faq.q: What is the origin of Badshah?
faq.a: Badshah is associated with Persian. Persian bādshāh ('king, emperor'), from bād ('lord') and shāh ('king'). The source record classified it as Arabic, which is incorrect.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Badshah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Badshah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Badshah is rendered بادشاه and carries the sense پادشاه، سلطان، فرمانروا.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Badshah, badshah. Script forms are بادشاه, بادشاہ, बादशाह.

faq.q: Is Badshah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
